newsitem.title: UK: Willis says no plans to replace Taylor.
newsitem.headline: Willis says no plans to replace Taylor.

text.p: Insurance broker Willis Corroon Group Plc said on Wednesday it has no plans to replace executive director Max Taylor, who has been nominated to succeed Sir David Rowland as chairman of Lloyd's at the end of this year.
"It's not as if we have to make a decision before the summer holidays. He'll be here for another six months," a spokesman for Willis Corroon told Reuters.
Instead of replacing Taylor, who does not have a line management role, his responsibilities at Willis will probably be distributed among his colleagues, the spokesman added.

Lloyd's announced earlier that Taylor, subject to his being appointed to the insurance market's ruling Council, will succeed Rowland, who is retiring after helping to rescue Lloyd's from record losses.
Willis is headed by executive chairman John Reeve and two executive directors, Taylor and Ken Pinkston.
